speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry will consider piloting the installation of sensor-activated alarm systems in HDB studio apartments for the elderly or in new HDB flats catered for the elderly; and (b) what will be the estimated cost increase for such installations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Other options include wearable devices with panic buttons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I understand that some Executive Condominium (EC) developers also have some of these products and suites available but the purchase by residents have been low.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I think the cost is about $6,000 to $8,000 for such applications.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It does not sound very expensive compared to the overall cost of the housing unit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even after that, you need to talk to their families to get the sense of whether there is someone that the system can auto-dial to and alert, or whether their neighbours who would respond or there are service providers who are monitoring the system and to be able to respond.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But these things can be worked out through various packages and, ultimately, it is awareness and it is about whether the seniors' caregiving arrangements and caregivers find value in having such a system as a protective factor for them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Has the Ministry considered this technology that is quite widespread, I believe, in Japan, which is attached to the hot water pot?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It monitors the frequency at which an elderly resident consumes hot water.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When they do not consume for a while, it sends a short message service (SMS) alert to their next-of-kin.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Apparently, this is widely used in Japan, it is very economical.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And is that being considered to be something that can be pushed out here?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are a variety of systems out there in the market, as well as a whole suite of projects that technopreneurs and researchers are working on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are some which are attached to their wrists and they can then press if there is an issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some are attached to phones or part of a phone app and if it detects a sudden drop in height, it will send out an alert message.
